correctness.rationale: The proxy event has a disjoint binomial complement, and the delegator event is exactly the mixture of opposite-proxy and same-proxy tie probabilities. Exact-rational exhaustive counterfactual enumeration checks both independently for m=1,3,5,7 and five values of p. Monotone likelihood/binomial factor arguments prove sharp finite-m optimization; central binomial asymptotics and an exponentially vanishing fixed-p correction prove the limit. The proof handles all parameter boundaries and asserts no even-m case.

originality.rationale: The original bipartite proxy model and its general evaluation algorithm are properly credited. The new result is not a restatement of computability: it proves explicit two-proxy all-parameter binomial formulas and a sharp uniform-in-delegation-propensity normalized upper envelope with an all-size limit. Fixed-delegation power and one-proxy power have different hypotheses and do not entail the disagreement/tie-mode argument. Searches did not yield a statement covering the exact analytic theorem; this is evidence, not a logical proof of novelty.
residual_risks: A specialized publication deriving the same two-proxy closed forms or an equivalent sharp uniform power bound may have escaped the indexed and direct literature searches.

A future comparison may reveal that the sharp asymptotic bound has already been extracted from general bipartite proxy-voting recurrences; the prior computation theorem alone did not state that consequence.
The 2026 network-centrality item was compared at summary level only and concerns expected delegation weight, rather than the present pivotality functional.

value.rationale: Two independently voting representatives form the smallest nontrivial competition for delegated votes. Although each receives linearly many delegated votes for fixed positive propensity, its normalized Penrose–Banzhaf power is universally forced to vanish; the exact optimal constant and all-size formulas identify the structural dilution mechanism. This meaningfully separates weight accumulation from decisive influence and contrasts one-representative concentration rather than merely substituting into a general numerical recurrence.
